title: Good Faith & Price Estimates Held by One Patient
content:
**Standard.** Under Good Faith & Price Estimates a patient may hold any number of estimates — there is no limit per patient — one estimate per scheduled service. A recurring course of care is one estimate covering at most the recurring-course maximum of its estimate type (twelve months), and a new estimate is opened when the course runs past that period. A change to an already estimated service is a new version of the same estimate, never a second estimate. An unscheduled price request becomes the estimate of the service once that service is scheduled.

## The same rule, case by case

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Two different services scheduled for one patient | two estimates, one per scheduled service |
| The date, items or providers of an estimated service change | a new version of the same estimate |
| A recurring course continues past the recurring-course maximum | a new estimate is opened for the period that follows |
| A patient who asked for a price without a date then schedules that service | the price request becomes the estimate of that service |

## Examples (hypothetical)

- A patient holds an estimate for an imaging study and books an unrelated outpatient procedure: the procedure receives its own estimate; the imaging estimate is unchanged.
- A patient's physical-therapy course is planned for sixteen months: one estimate covers the first twelve months, and a new estimate is opened when the course runs past them.
